attributes.readMe:
## Case

Tickets are units of conversation; a Case is the unit of accountability — one customer problem spanning tickets, days, and owners, with severity, findings, and a resolution record. It LINKS the related tickets (reusing the existing Ticket block) rather than replacing them.

```ts
import { Case } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/service-desk/case';

@field case = linksTo(() => Case);
```

### Composition

A Case is built from the catalog's record fields: `caseId` (Record Identifier), `ownership` (Record Owner, written by Assign Owner — which also sets the `owner` link, so the two agree), `relationships` (Relationship Set), `externalRefs` (External Reference) and `workflowState` (Workflow State). Around it sit the other case records, each linking **up** to the case: Customer Replies, Escalations and an applied SLA.

### Two lifecycles, on purpose

`status` is the case's outcome — open, investigating, waiting on the customer, resolved, closed — and Resolve Case writes it. `workflowState` is where the case sits in a team's own Workflow, and Run Workflow writes it. A team that guards its resolved state runs the case through Run Workflow as well as Resolve Case; the outcome and the process position are read separately.

### Examples

An investigation not yet in the workflow (`Case/checkout-outage-investigation`), cases being worked and newly opened (`case-2026-0142`, `case-2026-0152`), one waiting on the customer (`case-2026-0160`) and one resolved (`case-2026-0131`).

### Non-goals

The SLA clock belongs to the applied SLA card, not the case: a case is judged by resolution quality, and its SLA by time. No customer-visible portal view.
